the development of a high frequency (45 MHz) ultrasound imaging system that can be used to image the human hand.

the design, development, and evaluation of a high-frequency phased array beamforming system that uses a sub-Nyquist, variable sampling method to generate high-resolution, broadband images of biological targets.
the design, implementation, and testing of a sub-Nyquist, variable sampling, high-frequency phased array beamformer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a sub-Nyquist, variable sampling, high-frequency phased array beamformer that has been implemented on an FPGA and tested with a 45-MHz phased array.

the beamforming method is a viable solution to the problem of high-frequency phased array beamforming and that it can be used to implement a high-frequency phased array system with a low-cost digital signal processor.

we have developed and implemented an advanced digital receive beamformer that is capable of real-time imaging of a 128-line 512-pixel image with a dynamic range of approximately 55 dB, a variable sampling factor of 1/3, and a maximum bandwidth of 83.0%, all in a 45-MHz, 64-element, 2-D phased array.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beamformer is capable of imaging with a 1:1 sampling rate and a 3:1 sampling rate.
the variable sampling beamformer is a viable alternative to the Nyquist sampling beamformer for imaging at high center frequencies.

the proposed beamforming method is capable of producing high quality images at a significantly lower cost and with significantly reduced computational complexity than the previously described systems.
